verdict: real failure: the part came off the sheet on the first layers
printer: Prusa CORE One, 0.6 mm nozzle, Buddy camera via go2rtc (1920x1080), textured sheet
part: 3423-TOP-REV F, the top (lid) of a jar, printed opening-down without supports
fault: a wrong-material print: the G-code was sliced with the Prusament PLA profile (215-220 °C nozzle, 60 °C bed) while Elegoo Rapid PETG was loaded, on the textured sheet. The rim ring did not bond and was dragged off its place by the nozzle a few layers in
what_it_looks_like: the ring, printed at the back centre, appears about 300 px to the right in the next frame; the bed only moves in Z, so a part that moves sideways has come loose
fixable_by_the_agent: no: nothing reattaches a detached part, and the material mismatch was invisible to the agent

expected_agent_action.at_the_first_visible_failure: pause and leave it for a person; cancel is also acceptable
never: temperature, fan, flow or speed changes

agent_turn: printobserver's agent saw the detachment in the first frame that showed it, took one look and paused at about 18:25:49, then held the pause until a person cancelled. It did not notice the material mismatch

first_visible_failure.what_shows_it: The rim ring that sat at the back-centre in frames 7-8 is now about 300 px to the right, beside the nozzle, on a sheet that only moves in Z. A part that changes XY position between frames has come off the bed and is being dragged. The short dark strand right of the nozzle has also gone. Frame 8 shows a wider glossy band on the ring's front edge, but the ring has not moved and the band fits a wall a few layers taller, so it is not a usable warning; reading it as lifting is hindsight at best.

right_action: Pause the print at once (agent-009) and escalate for a person: the part is off the sheet in the first few layers, so nothing is salvageable and no temperature, fan, flow or speed change can reattach it. A person must clear the filament from the nozzle, clean the sheet and cancel. Cancelling outright would also be acceptable, since every remaining layer would be laid onto nothing, but pause-and-escalate is preferred so a person can inspect the nozzle. It must not take several more looks first: each minute of printing winds more filament around the nozzle.
agent_did: The agent called the start-up and first-layer frames correctly, recognised the detachment at the first frame that showed it (18:24:50), took one confirming look and paused at about 18:25:49 with escalation, then held the pause until a person cancelled. That was right and fast, but like everyone else it did not notice the material mismatch (it called 220 °C normal).
labelling_notes: Frames are 1920x1080, not the stated 1280x720. Rows 1-4 share agent turns with their looks, as do 5-6, 7-8 and 9-11. The G-code fields drift after the pause (z 1.6 to 2.0, progress 3.1 to 5.2 while paused), probably because of buffered moves and how the packet sampled position, so the camera is the better clock here. When the ring was dragged, the G-code was already at z 1.6 with solid infill in the layer: the base ring had a few layers, but on camera it never got past a thin first-layer ring. Root cause, from the case description: Elegoo PETG printed with the Prusament PLA profile (about 215-220 °C nozzle and 60 °C bed), which gives weak first-layer adhesion. Nothing in the frames shows the wrong material before the detachment.

A periodic observation of the first layer going down at the back centre, before anything has moved; the agent should carry on and change nothing.
